title: Quantum Simulation of Two-Dimensional Free Dirac Hamiltonian in Multimode Circuit QED
authors: Jiwon Kang, Jiuk Lee, Eliya Blumenthal, Shay Hacohen-Gourgy, Eunseong Kim
abstract: Two-dimensional massive Dirac systems feature a gapped Dirac-cone dispersion central to a broad range of phenomena in condensed-matter and topological physics. While quantum simulations have demonstrated one-dimensional Dirac dynamics and two-dimensional massless Weyl dynamics, programmable simulation of massive two-dimensional Dirac dynamics remains experimentally unexplored. Here, we realize a programmable two-dimensional free Dirac Hamiltonian in circuit QED, with independently tunable spin-momentum couplings and mass, using a single Rabi-driven qubit coupled to two modes of a multimode cavity. Using this Hamiltonian, we observe rotational Zitterbewegung of a two-dimensional massive Dirac particle and its dependence on the effective mass. Time-dependent master-equation simulations incorporating measured decoherence, corrections beyond the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), and anharmonicity of the transmon reproduce the observed dynamics. Our results establish multimode circuit QED as a compact, programmable platform for higher-dimensional relativistic quantum dynamics and provide a foundation for exploring dynamical and topological phenomena in gapped Dirac systems.
summary: The research demonstrates the realization of a programmable two-dimensional free Dirac Hamiltonian using circuit QED. By coupling a transmon qubit to a multimode cavity, the authors simulate the dynamics of massive Dirac particles, observing characteristic Zitterbewegung. This establishes the platform as a powerful tool for studying higher-dimensional relativistic quantum phenomena.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the programmable quantum simulation of two-dimensional massive Dirac dynamics, a regime that has not been experimentally explored despite successes in 1D and massless 2D simulations.
main_result: The authors successfully realized a programmable 2D free Dirac Hamiltonian in circuit QED, observing rotational Zitterbewegung and confirming the platform's utility for higher-dimensional relativistic quantum dynamics.
method: The simulation relies on engineering the Hamiltonian using a single transmon qubit coupled to two modes of a multimode cavity, with dynamics analyzed via time-dependent master-equation simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a circuit QED setup using a transmon qubit coupled to a multimode cavity. The dynamics are governed by an effective Dirac Hamiltonian, which is programmed by tuning the qubit-cavity couplings and detunings.
key_observables: Rotational Zitterbewegung of the Dirac particle, expectation values of cavity quadratures ($\langle\hat{X}_jangle$), and time-averaged fidelity.
important_parameters: Effective mass (tunable via detuning $\Delta\Omega$), Rabi frequencies ($\Omega_R$), cavity mode coupling strengths ($\chi_j$), and decoherence times ($T_{1,ho}, T_{2,ho}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis incorporates corrections beyond the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA), finite transmon anharmonicity, and measured decoherence effects, which are key limitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy-level diagram, the schematic of the Dirac Hamiltonian dynamics, the experimental setup, and time evolution plots comparing experimental data to master-equation simulations for Zitterbewegung.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical realization of the 2D Dirac Hamiltonian, presents calibration procedures for drive amplitudes and phases, demonstrates the measurement protocol using characteristic functions, and finally analyzes the resulting Zitterbewegung dynamics while accounting for decoherence and anharmonicity.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of quantum simulation in circuit QED, demonstrating control over complex, relativistic Hamiltonians (like the massive Dirac equation) in a solid-state platform, which is a major goal in AMO physics.
